find: For Edexcel 1ET0 Component 2, Section A, you will answer a two-part question on Jekyll and Hyde. Part (a) asks you to analyse an extract of around 400 words, focusing on language and how Stevenson creates meaning (AO1 + AO2). Part (b) asks you to explore a theme, character, or idea across the whole novella (AO1 + AO2).
replace: For the Edexcel 19th-century novel question you answer two parts on Jekyll and Hyde. Part (a) prints an extract of about 400 words and is worth 20 marks for close analysis of Stevenson’s language, form and structure (AO2). Part (b) is worth 20 marks and asks you to explore a theme, character or idea across the whole novella, judged on your argument and your use of quotations (AO1).
note: F1: part (a) assesses AO2 only and part (b) AO1 only; the old text gave both parts AO1 + AO2. Also removes two banned strings.

Explore how Stevenson uses language to present Jekyll’s attitude at this point in the novella.

find: Jekyll’s statement ends mid-sentence. He writes: “I bring the life of that unhappy Henry Jekyll to an end.”
replace: Jekyll’s statement ends with one calm, final sentence: “Here then, as I lay down the pen and proceed to seal up my confession, I bring the life of that unhappy Henry Jekyll to an end.”
note: F4: the confession ends with a complete sentence, not mid-sentence.

expect: Mid-sentence — "I bring the life of that unhappy Henry Jekyll to an end."
value: With one calm final sentence — "I bring the life of that unhappy Henry Jekyll to an end."
note: F4: same correction as the content fix.

find: Eight months later, Hyde commits a far more terrible crime.
replace: Nearly a year later, Hyde commits a far more terrible crime.
note: F5: Chapter 4 opens 'Nearly a year later, in the month of October'.

find: The contrast is striking: half the rooms are furnished with luxury and good taste, while the other half are in disarray, with clothes thrown on the floor and a pile of ash in the fireplace where Hyde has been burning papers.
replace: The contrast is striking: the two rooms Hyde uses are furnished “with luxury and good taste,” yet they have been hurriedly ransacked, with clothes thrown on the floor and a pile of ash in the fireplace where papers have been burned.
note: F6: Hyde used only a couple of rooms; the disorder is a hurried ransacking, not a second half of the flat.

expect: Half luxurious and tastefully furnished; half chaotic, with burnt papers in the fireplace.
value: Rooms furnished with luxury and good taste, yet hurriedly ransacked with burnt papers in the fireplace.
note: F6: same correction as the content fix.

find: The maidservant is one of only two women in the entire novella (the other is the girl Hyde tramples).
replace: The maidservant is one of only a handful of women in the novella; the others are the girl Hyde tramples and the old woman who keeps his Soho rooms.
note: F7: the Soho housekeeper is a third named woman, so 'only two' is false.

find: She watches the murder from a window “romantically given” and by the light of a full moon.
replace: She is “romantically given,” and she watches the murder from her window by the light of a full moon.
note: F8: the phrase is applied to the maid in the text, not to the window.
F9: the text reads 'looking deathly sick'.
F10: the novella has 'Something troglodytic'; 'troglodyte' never appears.
F10: same misquotation.
F10: same misquotation.

find: Jekyll’s house is in a wealthy, respectable area (loosely based on Cavendish Square).
replace: Jekyll’s house stands on an unnamed square of “ancient, handsome houses” — Cavendish Square, the one square Stevenson names, is where Lanyon lives.
note: F11: the novella puts Lanyon in Cavendish Square; Jekyll's square is never named.

expect: In which respectable London square does Stevenson place Jekyll's front entrance?
value: What kind of square does Stevenson put Jekyll's front entrance on?
note: F11: the card taught Cavendish Square as Jekyll's address.

expect: A wealthy square modelled loosely on Cavendish Square.
value: An unnamed square of ancient, handsome houses, most of them now decayed and let out as flats.
note: F11: same correction as the question.

find: When the fog lifts briefly during the Carew murder, the moonlight reveals the violence that normally remains hidden.
replace: On the night of the Carew murder the fog has not yet come down, and the full moon lights the lane so brightly that the maid sees everything.
note: F12: the text says the early part of that night was cloudless and the fog rolled in later.

expect:
